hook.text: When a car turns, the outside wheel travels farther than the inside one. They can't spin the same speed.

buildup.text: If both wheels were locked together, the car would judder and scrub its tires in every turn.

discovery.text: The differential is a gearbox between the wheels that lets them spin at different speeds.

twist.text: A basic diff sends power to the wheel with least resistance—bad when one tire is on ice.

climax.text: Limited-slip differentials solve this by locking partially, sending power where grip exists.

punchline.text: The diff lets your wheels disagree—politely.

quiz.question: What does a differential allow?
options: Wheels to spin at different speeds

details.summary: The differential is a gearbox between the drive wheels that allows them to rotate at different speeds during turns, preventing tire scrub and enabling smooth cornering on paved surfaces.
details.whyItMatters: Without a differential, the inner and outer wheels in a turn would be forced to spin at the same rate, causing tire wear, loss of grip, and poor handling on every corner.
takeaways: It splits engine torque between left and right drive wheels
Outer wheels travel farther and spin faster in turns
Limited-slip differentials improve traction on slippery surfaces

faq.question: What is a limited-slip differential?
faq.answer: A limited-slip differential transfers some torque from a spinning wheel to the one with better grip. This prevents one wheel from spinning uselessly while the other gets no power, improving traction.

faq.question: Do EVs have differentials?
faq.answer: Most do. EVs with a single motor use a simple reduction gear and differential. Dual-motor EVs with one motor per axle may not need a center differential since each motor independently drives its axle.
